xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4945: Agent MCP and bots (W-OAUTH1): OAuth 2.1 server for /mcp

plan.title: Agent MCP and bots (W-OAUTH1): OAuth 2.1 server for /mcp
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Hosted MCP clients (Claude Desktop connectors, Grok Bot, the xAI API) cannot be handed a token file; they expect the MCP authorization flow (discover, register, authorize, token). Overdeck's /mcp accepts only hand-made access tokens, so these clients cannot connect at all.
narratives.Proposal: Add an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for /mcp: RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 metadata, dynamic client registration, PKCE S256 authorize with an operator approval in the dashboard (approval code on the page and in the dashboard), a token endpoint issuing 30-day odk_ access tokens and rotating 90-day odr_ refresh tokens with reuse detection, revocation, root-only operator endpoints, a WWW-Authenticate challenge on the /mcp 401, and pan mcp oauth CLI verbs. Access tokens are ordinary kind:'token' registry records with oauthClientId, oauthFamilyId and expiresAt; families live in ~/.overdeck/mcp-oauth.json; approvals and codes live in memory. See .pan/drafts/PAN-4945.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No dashboard approval card or sign-in list UI (W-OAUTH2, PAN-4946)
- No Tailscale Funnel access, public switch, rate limits or Funnel audit entries; Funnel requests to the new routes must still get 404 (W-FUN1, PAN-4947)
- No change to remote-request-gate.ts or route-scopes.ts
- No CORS headers on the OAuth endpoints
- No socket close or revocation event when an OAuth token expires
- No custom URI-scheme redirect URIs, confidential clients, client secrets, client_credentials or password grants
- No OpenID Connect (openid-configuration, ID tokens)
- No change to routes/access-tokens.ts or src/cli/commands/token.ts
- No cli/mcp.mdx page (epic W-DOC)
- No token, refresh token, code or state value in any log line, URL other than the registered redirect, or error body

metadata.sizeJustification: One OAuth 2.1 authorization server is one security protocol: discovery, registration, authorize, token and revocation are useless alone, and the epic already split everything separable (W-OAUTH2 UI, W-FUN1 Funnel). The plan touches exactly 25 files; the subsystem count (7) exceeds 6 only because the lint counts each top-level doc file (configuration/mcp.mdx, docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md) as its own subsystem.

autoDecisions.summary: Issuer is matched from the request Host / X-Forwarded-Host against getTrustedOrigins() (Funnel requests use triggerFunnelBaseUrl); the epic's fixed 127.0.0.1 loopback branch is dropped.
autoDecisions.rationale: The MCP SDK (client/auth.js:344-357, shared/auth-utils.js:23-43) throws unless the advertised resource has the origin the client called; trusted origins already include http://localhost:<port> and http://127.0.0.1:<port>, and an allowlist never trusts an arbitrary Host.

autoDecisions.summary: state is optional at authorize; PKCE S256 is mandatory.
autoDecisions.rationale: The SDK sets state only when the provider supplies one (client/auth.js:732); OAuth 2.1 relies on PKCE for CSRF protection, so requiring state would break stock clients.

autoDecisions.summary: requestedLevel is the lowest level named in scope (default read); unknown scope names are ignored.
autoDecisions.rationale: A stock SDK client requests every scopes_supported value (client/auth.js:229), and the requested level becomes the approval card's default (W-OAUTH2), so the least-privilege reading is the safe default; RFC 6749 lets a server ignore unknown scopes.

autoDecisions.summary: Families keep up to 20 retired refresh hashes (priorRefreshHashes) and the current accessTokenId.
autoDecisions.rationale: The epic's single refreshHash cannot detect reuse after rotation; accessTokenId lets a refresh detect that the operator revoked the current access token through Settings or pan token revoke.

autoDecisions.summary: Revoking an OAuth access token through Settings → Access Tokens or pan token revoke ends the sign-in at its next refresh (no change to routes/access-tokens.ts or token.ts).
autoDecisions.rationale: pan token revoke writes the registry directly, so only a check at refresh time covers every revoke path.

autoDecisions.summary: Add pan mcp oauth pending, approve and deny beyond the epic's issue, list and revoke.
autoDecisions.rationale: The approval card is PAN-4946; without these verbs this slice's sign-in could be approved only with a hand-written curl and the internal token.

autoDecisions.summary: Loopback http redirect URIs match at authorize with any port; the token endpoint compares redirect_uri exactly.
autoDecisions.rationale: RFC 8252 §7.3 and OAuth 2.1 §8.4.2 require port flexibility for native loopback clients; the token endpoint must repeat the exact URI used at authorize.

autoDecisions.summary: client_name is optional and defaults to 'Unnamed MCP client'.
autoDecisions.rationale: RFC 7591 makes client_name optional; the name is self-declared and never trusted, so a default costs nothing.

autoDecisions.summary: The authorize page CSP adds connect-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri 'none' and form-action 'none' to the epic's CSP.
autoDecisions.rationale: default-src 'none' alone blocks the page's own status poll; the other directives stop framing and form or base hijacking.

autoDecisions.summary: Unused-client and ended-family pruning runs lazily on every store read and mutation; no new timer.
autoDecisions.rationale: The store is small and only the dashboard writes it; access-token pruning already rides the existing agent-token sweep.

autoDecisions.summary: Capacity: 50 clients (evict the oldest client without a family, refuse only when all have one) and 20 pending approvals (drop the oldest).
autoDecisions.rationale: Refusing at capacity would let any LAN or Funnel peer lock out registration; eviction only touches registrations that never completed a sign-in.

autoDecisions.summary: cli/mcp.mdx is left to the epic's W-DOC item; this issue documents the CLI in configuration/mcp.mdx.
autoDecisions.rationale: W-DOC creates cli/mcp.mdx together with the connector verbs; keeping two doc files keeps the plan inside the 25-file finalize limit.

narrative.Action: Execute PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4945.md WI-1 exactly. items.title: Given an OAuth token record with expiresAt in the future, verifyAccessToken returns ok; when Date passes expiresAt it returns { ok: false } and listActiveRecordsOfKind('token') omits it, while readActiveAccessTokenRecord still returns it

pruneEndedAccessTokens(7 days) deletes an OAuth record expired 8 days ago, preserves one expired 6 days ago, and preserves a plain token revoked 30 days ago

narrative.Action: Execute PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4945.md WI-4: create src/lib/mcp/oauth-service.ts with createMcpOAuthService(deps: now, randomBytes) and mcpOAuthService, implementing registerClient (D-4 incl. 50-client capacity with eviction of the oldest client without a family), authorize (D-5, D-6: in-memory approvals, 20 pending max, approval code), approvalStatus, listApprovals, decideApproval, exchangeCode (D-7: code consumed before checks, reused code revokes its family, mint access token then write family, revoke minted token if the family write fails). Never log a token.

items.title: Given register, authorize and approve at level operate, approvalStatus returns approved with a redirect carrying code and the original state, and exchangeCode returns tokens whose access token verifies with scopes read:state, read:conversations, tell, operate and an oauthClientId
exchangeCode rejects a wrong code_verifier with invalid_grant and then rejects the correct verifier for the same code with invalid_grant (the code is consumed)
exchangeCode rejects a code at now + 61 s with invalid_grant, and a second exchange of a used code returns invalid_grant and revokes the access token the first exchange produced
authorize returns an error-page (no redirect) for an unknown client_id or an unregistered redirect_uri, and a redirect carrying error=invalid_request for code_challenge_method=plain

approvalStatus returns expired at createdAt + 10 min + 1 s, decideApproval returns 409 for an already decided approval and 400 for approve without a level, and the 21st pending approval drops the oldest
Implement refresh rotation, reuse detection and revocation in the OAuth service

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Shares oauth-service.ts only with the authorize and admin service items, which blocks edges order before and after it.

narrative.Action: Execute PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4945.md WI-5 (D-8, D-9): add refresh, revokeToken and revokeFamily to the service, all run through one serialized queue. Rotation writes the new refresh hash, prepends the old one to priorRefreshHashes (max 20), sets accessTokenId, then revokes every other access record of the family. A retired refresh token revokes the family; a revoked current access record (outside revocation) revokes the family; a pruned (missing) current record does not.

items.title: refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token; the previous access token then fails verifyAccessToken and the new one verifies
When the first refresh token is presented again after rotation, refresh returns invalid_grant and afterwards both the newest access token and the newest refresh token are refused

After revokeAccessToken(<current access token id>) the next refresh returns invalid_grant and the family is marked revoked; when the current access record is missing from the registry, refresh still succeeds
refresh with a different client_id returns invalid_grant and preserves the family; refresh at refreshExpiresAt + 1 ms returns invalid_grant

Two concurrent refreshes with the same refresh token produce exactly one success and leave the family revoked; revokeToken resolves for 'garbage' and revokes the family for a Date-expired access token
